clue.text: Thriving business's current worry

parts.note: the going rate is the current one, so going means current
a concern is a worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: A company's present anxiety, perhaps about its own success.
explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is the accountants' term for a business trading profitably with every prospect of continuing.

clue.text: Decline to visit planter?

parts.note: to go to a place is to visit it
a plant pot is a planter, the question mark flagging the example

explanation.surface: Turning down an invitation to look round a garden container.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom meaning to deteriorate or decline.

clue.text: Maiden secured by one fairly good ball — never mind the others

indicators.note: secured by means the maiden letter is held by and follows the letter for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
all right means satisfactory or fairly good
the jack is the small target ball in bowls

explanation.surface: A cricketing over without runs, then a decent delivery: a bowler pleased with himself regardless of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored; in bowls, a British lawn game, the jack is the target ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The British catchphrase expresses smug selfishness: I am fine, so the others do not matter.

clue.text: Person beyond saving, individual imprisoned by King George

indicators.note: imprisoned by means the individual word is held inside the royal cipher

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
an individual is one, a single person

explanation.surface: A lost soul, one person jailed on the orders of King George.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone who is doomed or past help.

clue.text: One penning chapter finished a quick read?

indicators.note: penning means the word for one encloses the chapter letter, as a pen holds sheep

parts.note: taken as written
over means finished, ended

explanation.surface: Someone who writes one chapter and is done, after a speedy perusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a quick look or inspection, so a quick read of something, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Talk about bowler, say

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a bowler is a kind of hat, hence 'say' for an example

explanation.surface: Discussion about a cricket bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket; it is the round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal talk.

clue.text: Practical articles reproduced about electric current

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the current symbol
reproduced means the letters of articles are made again in a new order

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Practical news items copied about electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced' turns ARTICLES into REALISTC, and 'about' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means practical and sensible about what can actually be done.

clue.text: Summer residence may be converted into good clean flats

indicators.note: converted means the letters of the phrase are rebuilt into a new form, as a building is converted into flats

explanation.surface: An estate agent's idea: a summer house turned into tidy apartments.
explanation.definitionFit: Castel Gandolfo, near Rome, is the traditional summer residence of the Pope.

clue.text: Shelter made from loose stones found on bottom of tarn

parts.note: scree is a slope of loose stones on a mountainside

indicators.note: bottom of takes the last letter of tarn, as this is a down clue

explanation.surface: A hiker's refuge built of rubble found at the foot of a mountain lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A tarn is a small mountain lake, a word common in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen shelters or protects, as a windbreak does.

clue.text: Transport to school

definitions.meaning: a railway service carrying passengers or goods
to school someone is to teach or coach them

explanation.definitionFit: A railway train is a means of transport, and to train is to teach, as a school does.

clue.text: Daily, standing at a stop, caught bus

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning woman, also called a char or charlady in British usage
to ban something is to stop it
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleaner waiting at a stop catches her bus to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing at' is padding linking the pieces; a 'daily' is the British word for a cleaner who comes in every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for outings, so a kind of bus.

clue.text: Coward cut off returning to Scottish resort

indicators.note: returning means the word for cut off is read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off a branch
Troon is a seaside golfing resort on the Ayrshire coast

explanation.surface: Someone who ran away and was cut off while heading back to a Scottish holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Poltroon is an old word for an utter coward.

clue.text: Small in size, most of brood left inside

indicators.note: inside means the letter for left is placed within the shortened word
most of means the word for brood loses its last letter

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals born together

explanation.surface: A small animal, with most of its brood left inside the nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final R of LITTER, leaving LITTE; 'inside' puts L in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Little is a plain synonym for small in size.

clue.text: Spasmodic bird-watcher?

parts.note: a keen birder chasing rarities is known by a slang name that also suits someone given to jerky spasms

explanation.definitionFit: Keen British birders who rush to see rare birds are slangily called by this name, which also means one who jerks spasmodically.

clue.text: Tell all to turn up fresh

parts.note: to come is to arrive or turn up
clean means fresh, as fresh sheets are clean ones

explanation.surface: Instructions to reveal everything when arriving looking new.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for confessing everything.

clue.text: Lifted boa — constriction finally follows

indicators.note: follows means the last letter comes after the scarf word

parts.note: a boa is a long feathery scarf, a kind of stole

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of constriction

explanation.surface: A feather boa raised up, with a snake's squeeze coming afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The boa looks like a snake, the constriction confirming it, but here it is the fashion accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifted is slang for stolen, as in taking goods without paying.

clue.text: Investigation may give her scare

indicators.note: may give means the letters of her scare could yield another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: An inquiry that might frighten a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic investigation.

clue.text: Familiar with a hospital featured in large book

indicators.note: featured in means the hospital letter is placed within the book word

parts.note: a tome is a big heavy book
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Familiar with a hospital that appears in a weighty volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at home with something is to be comfortable and familiar with it.

clue.text: A plank on a yacht maybe

parts.note: a board is a plank of wood

explanation.surface: A single wooden plank on a sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on a ship or boat, of which a yacht is one example.

clue.text: Liking page's charm

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
to enchant is to charm

explanation.surface: Fondness for a page boy's charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or inclination for something.

clue.text: Recent plays by English dramatist

indicators.note: plays means the letters of recent move about freely

explanation.surface: Recent dramas by an English playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' and 'dramatist' suggest a theatre context, but plays is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman comic dramatist of the second century BC.

clue.text: Aim to lodge a protest

definitions.meaning: an aim is a goal or purpose
to raise an objection, to express disapproval formally

explanation.definitionFit: Object as a noun is a purpose or aim; as a verb it means to protest.

clue.text: Judge first half of recipe book

indicators.note: first half of takes the opening three of the six letters of recipe

parts.note: to book a table is to order or reserve it

explanation.surface: A judge sampling the opening section of a cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like a noun after 'recipe' but works as a verb, to order.
explanation.definitionFit: In England a recorder is a barrister sitting as a part-time judge in the Crown Court.

clue.text: Sounds like porridge for this conspirator?

indicators.note: sounds like means the word for porridge is spoken to give the name

parts.note: porridge is made from oats

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal giving its name to a plotter.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates fabricated the 'Popish Plot' of 1678; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates invented a Catholic conspiracy to kill Charles II, making him a notorious plotter.

clue.text: Pack needing to pull after onset of snow

indicators.note: after means the pull word follows the opening letter
onset of picks the first letter of snow

parts.note: to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: A sled team needing to pull once snow begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack things away.

clue.text: Runs round county town, town with a cathedral and castle

definitions.text: town with a cathedral and castle

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape
Chester is the county town of Cheshire

explanation.surface: Runs round the county town: a description of a Kent city with ancient landmarks.
explanation.walkthrough: A county town is the administrative centre of a British county; Chester serves Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester in Kent has a Norman cathedral and a famous castle keep.

clue.text: Short story being broadcast: The Claw

indicators.note: short means the story word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
a programme being broadcast is on, on air

explanation.surface: A short story airing on the radio called The Claw, like a horror title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims TALE to TAL; 'being broadcast' looks like a homophone signal but simply gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: A Wimbledon umpire should be well-informed

definitions.text: A Wimbledon umpire should be well-informed

parts.words: A Wimbledon umpire should be well-informed
parts.note: a tennis umpire literally must keep track of points, the phrase meaning to understand the real situation

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be aware of the true state of affairs, which a tennis umpire calling points literally is.
